svg.title: Developer journey — running the installer and answering its setup questions — A developer answers all the setup questions and builds the framework
svg.text: Developer journey — running the installer and answering
Scenario: A developer answers all the setup questions and builds the framework

g.text: Given a developer has just cloned a brand-new empty project into the
terminal
The empty copy (cloned from GitLab) as the developer sees it: git reports an empty project
with nothing saved yet. Set up off-screen: the test user, the installer, the tools it needs,
and the GitLab login.
When the developer starts the toolbox installer
The installer opens with its first question — install the complete framework? — with the
typed command still visible above it.
And the developer keeps the complete framework and the first question
asks about Ansible
Saying yes to the complete framework starts the setup questions from Copier (the tool that
builds the project from your answers); the first — does the project need Ansible? — defaults
to no.
And the developer keeps GitLab as the CI/CD platform
The next question asks which CI/CD platform to use — the automatic build-and-deploy system
that runs on every change; the developer keeps the default, GitLab.
And the developer keeps Docker as the container runtime
The next question asks which tool runs the containers; the developer keeps the default,
Docker.
And the developer keeps the generated docker-compose file
With Docker chosen, the setup offers to create project/docker-compose.yml; the developer
keeps the default, yes.
And the developer keeps the project workspace enabled
The next question turns the project workspace on or off (it adds project/Taskfile.yml and
docker-compose.yml); the developer keeps it on.
And the developer keeps Renovate auto-merge enabled
The next question asks whether Renovate — the bot that proposes dependency updates — should
merge toolbox updates on its own; the developer keeps it on.
And the developer keeps English as the Gherkin language
The last question sets the language for the test descriptions; the developer keeps the
default, en.
Then the installer builds the project and shows the finished screen
Answering the last question builds the framework and runs the setup to the finished screen.
The test also checks the log for the key lines (created files, scaffolded successfully,
Installation complete!).
And the project folder now holds the full DevSecOps framework
The project folder the questions produced — Taskfile.yml, .config, .gitlab-ci.yml, .agent
and more (listed without colour so nothing can tint a folder name). The test also lists the
folder to check the key files.
